Build Notes (Shared for all Variants)

The consensus Rogue meta build. One charged shot pierces an entire enemy line; with Eaglehorn the arrow bounces off walls and returns, so good angles hit the pack twice. Cross-checked across four sources: the freshest patch-3.1.2 class snapshot says Poison Penetrating Shot now leads the class, Maxroll's push list rates it S, Icy Veins' build list rates it S, and Maxroll's week-1 review reports Poison Penetrating Shot leading Tower leaderboards. Disagreement noted and not hidden: Maxroll's *overall endgame* list rates it only A tier, along with every other Rogue build - it has no Rogue build in S. The honest reading is that this build is exceptional at pushing and leaderboard play and merely very good at casual farming, and that it demands positioning discipline that a spin-and-win build does not.

Rotation
  1. Positioning is the build: fight with a wall behind or beside the pack so Eaglehorn's arrow bounces back through it.
  2. Penetrating Shot continuously down enemy lines, Forceful Arrow woven in for Energy, Poison Imbuement maintained by attacking, Shadow Clone on cooldown, Dash out of danger rather than through it.
Variants

Leveling — Poison Imbuement up, Forceful Arrow to refill Energy, then Penetrating Shot down the longest line of enemies you can find. Dash between packs. Shadow Clone on every elite.
Move on when Level 70 with Torment 1 unlocked - the endgame guide assumes exactly this starting point. Aspect of Imitated Imbuement must be in hand before you make the switch.

Early Endgame — Keep Poison Imbuement up by hitting things, not by waiting on the cooldown. Shadow Clone for the damage window and the Vulnerable application. Dash between packs to stack Ferocity. Penetrating Shot continuously down enemy lines. Talisman at this stage: Spellbound Steel, which applies Shadow Imbuement while you progress toward the real set.
Move on when You have the Sightless Set assembled - once Shadow Clone starts resetting rapidly the rotation changes character entirely.

Late Endgame — With the Sightless Set online, Shadow Clone comes back almost immediately - so lead every pack with it rather than saving it. Poison Imbuement is maintained by attacking. Note the Mythic budget: only ONE crafted Mythic can be equipped at a time, so Eaglehorn is the craft and everything else on this list has to drop. Since 3.1.2 you can recycle Mythics, so a wrong craft is recoverable.
Move on when Eaglehorn equipped and the Sightless Set complete - at that point start Pit and Tower pushing rather than farming.

Pushing — Positioning is the build. Fight with a wall behind or beside the pack so Eaglehorn's arrow bounces back through it for a second hit - Maxroll lists 'requires good positioning' as the build's stated downside, and at push tiers that is where the clear time is won or lost. Shadow Clone on cooldown, Poison Imbuement maintained by attacking, Dash out of danger rather than through it.

Stat requirements
  • Aim for 70% Critical Strike Chance on your character sheet while in town.
  • You only need 50% Attack Speed Bonus on gear, since 10 stacks of Ferocity grant another 50%.

Uniques
  • weapon Target-farm Echo of Varshan, an Initiate-tier Lair boss (1 Lair Key, Torment 1+ required) for the base bow, then craft the crafted-Mythic version via the Horadric Cube (4 Pandemonium Fragments) or the Jeweler — this build's crafted-Mythic priority #1. Where →
  • offhand Target-farm Harbinger of Hatred at Greater Lair tier (1 Greater Lair Key). Where →
  • offhand Target-farm The Butcher at Greater Lair tier (1 Greater Lair Key) — alternative to Etna's Lost Dagger from the same class of run. Where →
  • helm Mythic Unique — no dedicated boss; any boss (best odds Corrupted Reaper in the Pandemonium Threshold) can drop it, or craft it via the Horadric Cube (4 Pandemonium Fragments) or the Jeweler. Where →
  • gloves No dedicated boss — general unique pool. Farm via the Horadric Cube 'Upgrade to Unique' recipe (Common gloves + 1 Enhanced Primordial Dust + 10 Primordial Dust). Where →
  • chest Target-farm Harbinger of Hatred at Greater Lair tier (1 Greater Lair Key). Where →
  • Target-farm The Butcher, a Greater-tier Lair boss (1x Greater Lair Key) - the dedicated source for this item. Where →

A Reinforcement only ever casts the base version of its skill and gains nothing from its own passives.

How to run them

The Poison variant hires Subo and takes Incendiary Bolt, Scorched Earth, Snipe and Molotov. Scorched Earth is the reason: it makes enemies take roughly 30% more damage-over-time from you, and damage-over-time is what a Poison Imbuement build is. Reinforce with Varyana on Bloodthirst, with Penetrating Shot as the Opportunity trigger - the Rogue planner stores a real named trigger here, unlike the Druid's. Note the fork with the Cold variant, which hires Raheir instead. Icy Veins disagrees with both and pairs Subo with a Raheir/Bastion reinforcement off Dark Shroud; that is a genuine disagreement rather than a stage difference, and Bastion's 90% damage-reduction bubble is a fair trade if you are dying to burst. Remember a Reinforcement only casts the base version of its skill and gets nothing from its own passives.

Plan

Honest framing first, because it is the whole story here: **no Rogue build guide publishes War Plan picks.** The field exists on all eleven of Maxroll's Penetrating Shot planner profiles and every one of them is empty - seven activity trees, zero nodes selected - and neither Maxroll's nor Icy Veins' guide has a War Plans section at all. That is an authoring gap at the source, not something this site can research away. The system itself is real and worth using: at Tyrael's table in Temis you chain up to five endgame activities, each activity carries its own seven-level tree, and those trees only earn experience while the activity is part of an active plan. The picks below are therefore Maxroll's build-agnostic Season 14 progression priorities, ordered for what this build actually needs - not a Rogue-specific plan anyone published.

What is lit9 picks recorded on 6 of 7 activities. Everything else is dimmed, not ruled out: the trees below are the game's own 100 nodes, and a War Plan is per character.
Build Notes (Shared for all Variants)

The consensus Rogue meta build. One charged shot pierces an entire enemy line; with Eaglehorn the arrow bounces off walls and returns, so good angles hit the pack twice. Cross-checked across four sources: the freshest patch-3.1.2 class snapshot says Poison Penetrating Shot now leads the class, Maxroll's push list rates it S, Icy Veins' build list rates it S, and Maxroll's week-1 review reports Poison Penetrating Shot leading Tower leaderboards. Disagreement noted and not hidden: Maxroll's *overall endgame* list rates it only A tier, along with every other Rogue build - it has no Rogue build in S. The honest reading is that this build is exceptional at pushing and leaderboard play and merely very good at casual farming, and that it demands positioning discipline that a spin-and-win build does not.

Rotation
  1. Positioning is the build: fight with a wall behind or beside the pack so Eaglehorn's arrow bounces back through it.
  2. Penetrating Shot continuously down enemy lines, Forceful Arrow woven in for Energy, Poison Imbuement maintained by attacking, Shadow Clone on cooldown, Dash out of danger rather than through it.
Variants

Leveling — Poison Imbuement up, Forceful Arrow to refill Energy, then Penetrating Shot down the longest line of enemies you can find. Dash between packs. Shadow Clone on every elite.
Move on when Level 70 with Torment 1 unlocked - the endgame guide assumes exactly this starting point. Aspect of Imitated Imbuement must be in hand before you make the switch.

Early Endgame — Keep Poison Imbuement up by hitting things, not by waiting on the cooldown. Shadow Clone for the damage window and the Vulnerable application. Dash between packs to stack Ferocity. Penetrating Shot continuously down enemy lines. Talisman at this stage: Spellbound Steel, which applies Shadow Imbuement while you progress toward the real set.
Move on when You have the Sightless Set assembled - once Shadow Clone starts resetting rapidly the rotation changes character entirely.

Late Endgame — With the Sightless Set online, Shadow Clone comes back almost immediately - so lead every pack with it rather than saving it. Poison Imbuement is maintained by attacking. Note the Mythic budget: only ONE crafted Mythic can be equipped at a time, so Eaglehorn is the craft and everything else on this list has to drop. Since 3.1.2 you can recycle Mythics, so a wrong craft is recoverable.
Move on when Eaglehorn equipped and the Sightless Set complete - at that point start Pit and Tower pushing rather than farming.

Pushing — Positioning is the build. Fight with a wall behind or beside the pack so Eaglehorn's arrow bounces back through it for a second hit - Maxroll lists 'requires good positioning' as the build's stated downside, and at push tiers that is where the clear time is won or lost. Shadow Clone on cooldown, Poison Imbuement maintained by attacking, Dash out of danger rather than through it.

Stat requirements
  • Aim for 70% Critical Strike Chance on your character sheet while in town.
  • You only need 50% Attack Speed Bonus on gear, since 10 stacks of Ferocity grant another 50%.
